topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: CPU Proximity
explanation:
Modern computer systems utilize a memory hierarchy to bridge the speed gap between CPU and main memory.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of storage with varying speeds and capacities.  Faster, smaller caches (L1, L2, etc.) store frequently accessed data closer to the CPU, while slower, larger main memory stores the rest. Effective caching strategies minimize memory access time and improve performance.  Cache misses, when data is not found in a cache, significantly impact performance, making cache management crucial for system optimization.
